recent_posts.title: Ubuntu’s old Unity desktop remade in Wayfire and Libadwaita
recent_posts.summary: A Ubuntu community member named Muqtxdir has created an experimental recreation of Ubuntu's discontinued Unity desktop using Wayfire compositor and Libadwaita widgets via gtk4-layer-shell. The demo shows a working launcher, dock, and panel that are recognisably Unity-inspired but with a flatter, modern look and background blur. The project is a personal experiment rather than a formal revival effort, but demonstrates that a modern Unity-style desktop is technically achievable with current Linux desktop tooling.

recent_posts.title: gThumb is barely recognisable in its GTK4/libadwaita port
recent_posts.summary: gThumb 4.0 alpha has been rewritten in Vala and ported to GTK4/libadwaita, resulting in a significantly redesigned UI. The update brings better spacing, clearer hierarchy, and new features including WEBP/PNG animation support, JXL export, and a censor filter. Some existing features like web albums, contact sheets, and the find-duplicates tool were dropped in this alpha. The app remains a viable alternative to cloud photo services for privacy-conscious users or DSLR shooters.

recent_posts.title: Attack knocks Ubuntu websites, services and Snap store offline
recent_posts.summary: Canonical's Ubuntu websites and services, including the Snap store, Launchpad, and several ubuntu.com subdomains, have been knocked offline by a sustained, cross-border attack since around 6PM UK time on April 30. Canonical is working to address the issue. Ubuntu APT repositories remain accessible via mirrors, and the OS itself is not compromised. A hacktivist group has reportedly claimed responsibility, though Canonical has not confirmed this. Users can monitor recovery progress at status.canonical.com.

recent_posts.title: Linux App Release Roundup (April 2026)
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of notable Linux application releases from April 2026. Highlights include Zed text editor reaching v1.0 with DeepSeek AI model support and improved Git integration; Shotcut 26.4 adding Vulkan GPU acceleration for speech-to-text; PeaZip 11.0 with up to 94% faster large archive pre-parsing; Scribus 1.7.3 gaining real-time spell checking in a separate thread; BleachBit 6.0 launching a new cookie manager; VirtualBox 7.2.8 adding Linux 7.0 kernel support; and Kdenlive 26.04 introducing monitor mirroring and animated transition previews. Other minor updates include LibreOffice 26.2.3, OpenShot proxy workflow, and Rio terminal v0.4.0.

recent_posts.title: Linux Mint’s new HWE ISOs improve hardware support
recent_posts.summary: Linux Mint has released new HWE (Hardware Enablement) ISO images for version 22.3 to address compatibility issues with newer hardware. The standard ISO ships with Linux kernel 6.14, which may lack support for components released after that kernel. The new HWE ISO includes Linux kernel 6.17, and the team plans to publish updated HWE ISOs each time a new HWE kernel lands in the distro. A Linux 7.0 HWE ISO is expected in summer 2026. Existing installs already receive HWE kernel updates automatically; the new ISOs are primarily for fresh installations on newer hardware.

recent_posts.title: How to run Ubuntu and Steam on a PS5 using a hypervisor exploit
recent_posts.summary: Security engineer Andy Nguyen has released a public project enabling PS5 Phat consoles on firmware 3.xx or 4.xx to boot Linux, including Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. The ps5-linux project exploits a patched hypervisor vulnerability to give Linux direct hardware access to the PS5's Zen 2 CPU and RDNA 2 GPU. Once running, users can install Steam and play games like GTA V Enhanced at 60fps/1440p with ray tracing. The setup requires building a bootable USB image via Docker, a 64GB+ USB drive, USB ethernet/Wi-Fi adapter, and keyboard/mouse. Limitations include a 60Hz output cap, no built-in Bluetooth, and the need to re-run the exploit after each reboot since it doesn't replace the stock ProsperoOS.

recent_posts.title: How to enable Ubuntu Pro in the new Security Center app on Ubuntu 26.04
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS removes the Software & Updates utility from default installs and moves Ubuntu Pro configuration into the Security Center app. The new enrollment flow is cleaner, with a prominent 'enable Ubuntu Pro' button that authenticates via Ubuntu One in a browser. Once enrolled, users can toggle Extended Security Maintenance (ESM) for thousands of packages, kernel live-patching, and Livepatch status in the top bar. The Security Center snap also works on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. A known bug showing 'Not available for this version' can be fixed by running `sudo snap connect desktop-security-center:system-observe` in the terminal.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu 16.04 LTS security support has ended – unless you pay
recent_posts.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 LTS (Xenial Xerus) Extended Security Maintenance (ESM) ended in April 2026, leaving systems without security updates. Users can upgrade through multiple stages (16.04 → 18.04 → 20.04 → 22.04 → 24.04) or pay for Canonical's Legacy add-on through Ubuntu Pro, which extends coverage until April 2031 for an additional fee. The Legacy ESM add-on is not included in standard Ubuntu Pro subscriptions and costs extra. Commands to check Pro status and enable legacy add-ons are provided.

recent_posts.title: Canonical is ‘ramping up’ AI in Ubuntu this year
recent_posts.summary: Canonical VP of Engineering Jon Seager has outlined plans to integrate AI features into Ubuntu in 2026, emphasizing a principled, local-first approach. AI additions will come in two forms: implicit features (e.g., on-device text-to-speech for accessibility) and explicit features (e.g., generative text, automated file management agents). The company favors local inference using open-weight models like Qwen and DeepSeek via its inference snaps. Ubuntu is also being shaped into an agentic-friendly OS using Snap confinement for secure agent workflows. Notably, there will be no AI kill-switch, and while AI won't replace Canonical employees, engineers proficient with AI tools are seen as more valuable. The approach is described as measured and value-driven rather than AI-for-AI's-sake.

recent_posts.title: Firefox 151 will let users choose VPN server location manually
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla is adding server location selection to Firefox's built-in free VPN, expected in Firefox 151 releasing May 19. The feature currently routes traffic through Fastly proxy servers automatically based on proximity, but users will soon be able to manually choose from supported locations: USA, UK, France, Canada, and Germany. The free VPN requires a Mozilla account, offers 50 GB/month, and only protects in-browser traffic. Android support is also planned with the same feature set.
